name: Vault
tagline: Stores secrets encrypted, issues short-lived credentials, audits every access.
whatItIs: HashiCorp Vault is an identity-based secrets manager. It encrypts secrets at rest, issues short-lived credentials on demand and records every access.

howItWorks.title: Barrier, seal and unseal
howItWorks.body:
Storage holds only ciphertext sealed by the barrier key.
operator init splits the root key into N Shamir shares.
K shares unseal; the key then lives only in memory.
Auto-unseal hands the root key to a KMS or HSM.
vault operator seal locks everything instantly.

howItWorks.title: Raft integrated storage
howItWorks.body:
Data is replicated on each node; no external database.
One active leader writes; standbys forward or redirect.
A majority commits each write: 2 of 3, 3 of 5.
Port 8200 serves the API, 8201 serves cluster traffic.
vault operator raft snapshot save captures a restorable backup.

howItWorks.title: Auth, tokens and policies
howItWorks.body:
AppRole gives machines a role ID plus a secret ID.
Login returns a token with policies and a TTL.
Policies list paths and capabilities; everything else is denied.
KV v2 paths need the data/ and metadata/ prefixes.

howItWorks.title: Secrets engines and leases
howItWorks.body:
KV v2 keeps versions with soft delete and rollback.
The database engine creates a unique user per request.
Every dynamic secret carries a lease that is revoked on expiry.
Lease renew and revoke work per lease or per prefix.

howItWorks.title: Audit and injection
howItWorks.body:
Audit devices log each request; secret values are HMAC-hashed.
Agent auto-auths with AppRole and renews the token.
Agent templates write secrets to files for the app.
Rendered files refresh when the secret changes.

howItWorks.title: What sits in front
howItWorks.body:
Clients (users, apps, CI jobs) call the HTTPS API on port 8200.
A load balancer in the Edge layer can front several nodes and health-check /v1/sys/health.
A Kubernetes pod (Platform) can authenticate with its service account JWT.
CI authenticates with AppRole or JWT and gets a short-lived token per run.

howItWorks.title: What sits behind
howItWorks.body:
Raft integrated storage on local disk (Infrastructure) holds the encrypted data.
Auto-unseal can hand the root key to a cloud KMS or HSM.
The database engine creates per-request PostgreSQL users that expire on lease.
The PKI engine issues short-lived certificates for TLS and mTLS.
Delivery to apps: Agent sidecar or injector, Secrets Store CSI provider, or External Secrets Operator.

howItWorks.title: Alternatives
howItWorks.body:
OpenBao: choose it for a Vault-compatible fork under the Linux Foundation with the same API and CLI concepts.
Cloud secret managers (AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, Google Secret Manager): choose them for provider-managed storage.
SOPS: choose it to keep encrypted secrets in Git without a server.
Kubernetes Secrets with External Secrets Operator: choose it to sync from an existing store.

flow: Workload or Agent presents role ID and secret ID.
AppRole validates them and returns a scoped, expiring token.
The request carries the token to a secrets path.
Policy allows or denies the capability on that path.
KV returns a version, or the database engine mints a leased user.
The leader commits the write to a Raft quorum.
The audit device records the request, with values hashed.
Agent renders the secret to a file for the app.

deploy.summary: On-prem path: Raft node in Docker with TLS, then auth and secrets, then backup and injection.
prerequisites: Linux VM with Docker Engine and openssl
DNS name and static IP per node
Ports 8200 and 8201 open on the LAN
A PostgreSQL instance for dynamic secrets

steps.title: Prepare host, directories and TLS
steps.code:
sudo useradd --system --home /srv/vault --shell /usr/sbin/nologin vault
sudo mkdir -p /srv/vault/{config,data,tls,logs,backup}
sudo openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -nodes -days 365 \
  -keyout /srv/vault/tls/tls.key -out /srv/vault/tls/tls.crt \
  -subj '/CN=vault-1.example.internal' \
  -addext 'subjectAltName=DNS:vault-1.example.internal,IP:127.0.0.1,IP:<NODE_IP>'
sudo chown -R vault:vault /srv/vault && sudo chmod 600 /srv/vault/tls/tls.key
steps.note: Replace <NODE_IP> and the DNS name. Use an internal CA in production.

steps.title: Write the server config with Raft storage
steps.note: Repeat per node with its own node_id and addresses. disable_mlock is the documented choice for Raft.

steps.title: Open the firewall and run the container
steps.code:
sudo ufw allow from <LAN_CIDR> to any port 8200,8201 proto tcp
docker run -d --name vault --restart unless-stopped \
  --user "$(id -u vault):$(id -g vault)" -p 8200:8200 -p 8201:8201 \
  -v /srv/vault/config:/vault/config:ro -v /srv/vault/data:/vault/file \
  -v /srv/vault/tls:/vault/tls:ro -v /srv/vault/logs:/vault/logs \
  -v /srv/vault/backup:/vault/backup \
  hashicorp/vault:1.18.5 server
vault() { docker exec -i -e VAULT_ADDR=https://127.0.0.1:8200 \
  -e VAULT_CACERT=/vault/tls/tls.crt -e VAULT_TOKEN vault vault "$@"; }
steps.note: 8200 is the API, 8201 is node-to-node Raft traffic. Limit both to the cluster subnet. For a throwaway lab only: docker run --cap-add=IPC_LOCK -p 8200:8200 hashicorp/vault:1.18.5 server -dev.

steps.title: Initialise and unseal
steps.code:
vault operator init -key-shares=5 -key-threshold=3   # prints the unseal keys and root token once: hand each share to a different custodian
vault operator unseal   # run three times, one share each
export VAULT_TOKEN=<ROOT_TOKEN>
vault status
vault operator raft list-peers
steps.note: Give each share to a different custodian. Revoke the root token after setup.

steps.title: KV v2, policy and AppRole
steps.code:
vault secrets enable -path=secret kv-v2
vault kv put secret/myapp/config db_user=app db_pass='<VALUE>'
vault policy write myapp - <<'EOF'
path "secret/data/myapp/*"     { capabilities = ["read"] }
path "secret/metadata/myapp/*" { capabilities = ["list"] }
EOF
vault auth enable approle
vault write auth/approle/role/myapp token_policies=myapp token_ttl=1h \
  token_max_ttl=4h secret_id_ttl=10m secret_id_num_uses=1
vault read -field=role_id auth/approle/role/myapp/role-id
vault write -f -field=secret_id auth/approle/role/myapp/secret-id
steps.note: KV v2 policies target secret/data/... and secret/metadata/... A policy on secret/myapp/ matches nothing.

steps.title: Dynamic PostgreSQL credentials
steps.code:
vault secrets enable database
vault write database/config/appdb plugin_name=postgresql-database-plugin \
  allowed_roles=app-ro \
  connection_url='postgresql://{{username}}:{{password}}@db.example.internal:5432/appdb' \
  username=vaultadmin password='<ADMIN_PASSWORD>'
vault write -f database/rotate-root/appdb
vault write database/roles/app-ro db_name=appdb default_ttl=1h max_ttl=24h \
  creation_statements="CREATE ROLE \"{{name}}\" WITH LOGIN PASSWORD '{{password}}' VALID UNTIL '{{expiration}}'; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO \"{{name}}\";"
vault read database/creds/app-ro
steps.note: Each read mints a unique user that expires with its lease. rotate-root hides the admin password from humans.

steps.title: Audit device and Raft snapshot backup
steps.code:
vault audit enable file file_path=/vault/logs/audit.log
vault operator raft snapshot save /vault/backup/vault-$(date +%F).snap
# host crontab, token bound to a snapshot-only policy:
0 2 * * * docker exec -e VAULT_ADDR=https://127.0.0.1:8200 -e VAULT_CACERT=/vault/tls/tls.crt -e VAULT_TOKEN=<BACKUP_TOKEN> vault vault operator raft snapshot save /vault/backup/vault-$(date +\%F).snap
# restore: vault operator raft snapshot restore -force /vault/backup/<FILE>.snap
steps.note: If every audit device fails, Vault refuses requests. Copy snapshots off-host.

steps.title: Inject secrets with Agent
steps.note: Agent logs in, renews the token and rewrites the file when the secret changes. The app only reads a file.

verify: vault status: Initialized true, Sealed false, Storage Type raft.
vault operator raft list-peers: all nodes listed, one leader.
curl -s --cacert tls.crt https://vault-1.example.internal:8200/v1/sys/health returns 200 on the leader.
vault read database/creds/app-ro returns a new username each time.
tail /srv/vault/logs/audit.log shows each request as JSON.
pitfalls: Policies on secret/myapp miss KV v2; use secret/data/myapp.
Losing unseal shares or the snapshot loses all data.
A full audit disk blocks every request.
Standby nodes need leader_ca_cert or retry_join fails on TLS.
Use secret_id_num_uses=1; a reusable secret ID is a password.
Dev mode (vault server -dev) is in-memory and unsealed: lab use only, never production.
keyPoints: The barrier encrypts storage; Shamir shares or auto-unseal release the key.
Integrated Raft storage gives HA and needs quorum: three nodes.
AppRole proves identity; deny-by-default policies grant per-path capabilities.
KV v2 versions static secrets; dynamic engines mint leased credentials.
quickDeploy: Run Raft config in Docker with TLS
Create KV v2, policy and AppRole
Snapshot to disk and inject with Agent
osiNote: Serves an HTTPS API; Raft peers talk over TLS on 8201.
production: Run three or five Raft nodes; alert when quorum or leader is lost.
Use auto-unseal or custody Shamir shares; never keep all shares together.
Snapshot nightly with cron and ship copies off-host; test restore.
Enable two audit devices; alert on audit write failures.
Revoke the root token; use short TTLs and single-use secret IDs.
